comments.text:
Have we forgot this????? Ukraine gave up its nuclear weapons under the Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances, signed on December 5, 1994. This agreement was made between Ukraine, Russia, the United States, and the United Kingdom.



Key Points of the Agreement:

Ukraine Gave Up Nuclear Weapons



After the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, Ukraine inherited the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal (about 1,900 strategic nuclear warheads and thousands of tactical nukes).

Ukraine agreed to transfer these weapons to Russia for dismantling and join the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as a non-nuclear state.

Security Assurances Given to Ukraine



In exchange, Russia, the U.S., and the U.K. pledged to:

Respect Ukraine’s independence and sovereignty.

Refrain from using force or threats against Ukraine.

Not use economic pressure to influence Ukraine.

Seek UN Security Council assistance if Ukraine was threatened with nuclear force.

Refrain from using nuclear weapons against Ukraine.

Outcome & Violations:

Ukraine fully disarmed by 1996.

Russia violated the agreement by annexing Crimea in 2014 and later invading Ukraine in 2022.

The U.S. and U.K. condemned Russia’s actions but did not provide direct military intervention, leading to criticism of the effectiveness of the Budapest Memorandum.

comments.author: @有什麼潑什麼
comments.text:
在這場令人震驚的會談中，川普展現出極端傲慢的姿態，彷彿不是在與一個主權國家的領袖對話，而是在呵斥一名屈服於強權的臣屬。

從頭到尾，川普不僅毫無外交禮儀地不斷插嘴，甚至根本不讓澤倫斯基完整表達自己的立場。 每當澤倫斯基試圖闡述烏克蘭的處境與需求，川普便粗暴地打斷，用輕蔑的語氣反覆強調：「你沒有籌碼（You have no leverage）」，毫不掩飾他對烏克蘭的鄙視。這不僅是對澤倫斯基個人的羞辱，更是對烏克蘭這個正在承受戰火摧殘的國家的公然侮辱。

談判過程更是充滿單方面的壓迫與不對等。 美方派出了兩個人——川普與副總統范斯，而烏克蘭只有澤倫斯基一人孤軍奮戰。整場談話完全用英語進行，沒有即時翻譯，明顯就是故意讓澤倫斯基處於劣勢，迫使他在極度不公平的條件下應對美方的攻勢。

川普不只是要求烏克蘭在戰爭中向俄羅斯屈服，甚至變本加厲，提出一項喪權辱國的礦產協議，其條件之苛刻近乎掠奪，彷彿烏克蘭的土地與資源已經成為川普私人企業的獵物。他不斷施壓，要澤倫斯基在幾乎沒有談判空間的情況下簽署這份協議，將烏克蘭的關鍵資源拱手讓給美國財團，作為「交換」——交換什麼？是對美國軍援的一點施捨嗎？還是換取川普的一點點「恩賜」？

這樣的談話，已經不只是外交失禮，而是毫無遮掩的強權欺壓。美國過去曾經自詡為世界民主與自由的燈塔，但如今在川普的掌控下，這盞燈卻照出了極端現實的霸權嘴臉：弱者沒有發言權，只有順從的義務。

在這場不對等的較量中，澤倫斯基孤立無援，但他仍然堅持自己的底線，不願屈服。這場會談，沒有締造任何和平的可能，反而暴露了川普內心深處對國際秩序的藐視——在他的眼裡，所謂「盟友」，只是可以被利用的附庸；所謂「談判」，只是強者對弱者的威脅與剝削。

comments.text:
El Presidente Donald Trump habría girado en torno a una propuesta controvertida: el cese del conflicto con Rusia a cambio del acceso a las tierras raras de Ucrania, sin garantías concretas de seguridad para el país europeo. Este planteamiento, lejos de abordar una solución diplomática integral, parece reducir la paz a una transacción económica, priorizando intereses geopolíticos sobre la estabilidad regional. Cabe señalar que, desde el inicio de la guerra, Estados Unidos y la Unión Europea han sido acusados de alimentar indirectamente el conflicto mediante el envío masivo de armamento y apoyo financiero —superior a los 100,000 millones de dólares—, en lugar de impulsar vías de diálogo efectivas. Si bien este respaldo buscaba fortalecer la resistencia ucraniana, también prolongó las hostilidades, dejando al país en una posición frágil donde su soberanía territorial y recursos naturales están ahora en juego.
La discusión entre Zelensky y Trump reflejaría, así, una dinámica preocupante: la explotación de la crisis ucraniana como escenario de negocios, donde las tierras raras —esenciales para la tecnología y la industria militar— se convierten en moneda de cambio. Este enfoque no solo ignora las demandas de seguridad de Ucrania, sino que evidencia cómo las potencias occidentales podrían estar beneficiándose de un conflicto que contribuyeron a escalar.

Le pire dans cette affaire c'est que l'Ukraine n'a reçu que 84 milliards des Etats-Unis. 

Je cite :
Selon des sources du gouvernement fédéral américain , le Congrès a adopté cinq lois dites "d'appropriation supplémentaire" depuis l'invasion de 2022, allouant 174,2 milliards de dollars de fonds à l'Ukraine.

Un autre outil de suivi du gouvernement américain - qui compile des données provenant de plus de 20 entités de contrôle de l'ensemble du gouvernement - estime que le montant global est légèrement plus élevé, à savoir 182,8 milliards de dollars. Cela s'explique par le fait que le tracker inclut également des dons plus modestes effectués par d'autres agences gouvernementales, telles que l'Agence américaine pour les médias mondiaux (USAGM) ou l'Agence américaine pour la coopération internationale (ACEI). Media (USAGM) ou le ministère de la justice (DOJ).

Sur ces 182,8 milliards de dollars, seuls 83,4 milliards ont été déboursés, les 99,4 milliards restants n'ayant pas encore été engagés ou dont le paiement n'a pas encore été approuvé.

Tbf Elon Musk is just a wealthy US citizen, while Zelensky is the current sitting president of the nation Ukraine.

I'll provide an example to help explain the issue at hand:

_If you invite _*_random Joe_*_ into the office, would you expect him to wear a suit?_
*_Maybe, or maybe not. It generally depends._*
_I'd say if he's a responsible citizen, sure, but you never know with random Joe. Besides, random Joe is just some guy. What is he representing? Nothing besides himself, so if he presents himself unprofessionally, he's only (at worst) tanking his own reputation._

_However, if you invite _*_president Bob of Nation A,_*_ would you expect him to wear a suit?_
*_Absolutely, 100%. No ifs, no buts._*
_Bob is a president, he needs to be the most well-prepared and well-kitted human being of Nation A, as he is representing Nation A. If he does not show up with a suit, or is unprepared and generally incapable, Bob will literally run the reputation of an entire nation into the ground, as he is the person voted into power of nation A._
_He's the leader, and leaders must be as professional as possible, lest you come off as a poor, uncaring leader._

comments.text:
Summary for anyone else who is struggling to skim the point from this sea of deflection:

Zelensky opens with painting a picture of the gravity of war, the thousands of Ukrainians including children being held as prisoners of war and detailing the type of military support he is asking for. 

Trump expresses that he considers his predecessors to be incapable for spending so much on this war without getting much in return, and basically he wants to get rare earth (rare mineral mining licenses) from Ukraine to sell and use for military and AI. It all reeks of Elon musk, but exploiting countries resources in exchange for military support is business as usual for the US. 

However it turns out that he is not in fact offering military support, only diplomatic assistance in negotiating a peace treaty with Putin, and hints at some of the profits on the rare earth he plans to extract but he won’t  quantify. Zelensky points out that Putin has already signed no less than 25 ceasefires and broke them all, so for any peace efforts to be effective they will need to be able to leverage military power to back their position. 

Trump evades discussing even the possibility offering any military support, and dismisses all questions about it as if they were a trivial details, and repeatedly assures the audience that it is impossible that that Putin will break the peace treaty because unlike the other 25 ceasefires this one will be signed by HIM.

From here on it is a circular discussion, Zelensky and the press try to press him for tangible promises in case the peace treaty doesn’t work out, but trump is unwilling to entertain the possibility that his charisma alone is not enough to end the war (he claims to have already stopped many before they could have started like one just the other day between two countries he won’t name.)

The audience is not satisfied with his grandiose delusions of securing peace with his charisma alone, and they insist on asking relevant questions, he tries to deflect from the matter at hand by all means he can think of, and when Zelensky says that [signing over his country’s natural resources in exchange for an uncertain peace treaty] it’s a one sided deal, Trump gets frustrated and resorts to bullying him.

comments.text:
For the first time, I have seen an American president and defence secretary openly advocate for diplomacy, warning against war and especially World War III. This level of transparency is rare, and it stands in stark contrast to the long history of U.S. military interventions.

Decades of American warfare—from Vietnam to Iraq and Afghanistan—have followed the same pattern: massive expenditures, countless deaths, and, in the end, a withdrawal that leaves behind instability. These wars do not serve the interests of ordinary Americans. Instead, they enrich arms manufacturers and defense contractors while the cost is borne by the poor, who fill the ranks of the military.

The Russia-Ukraine conflict cannot be won by conventional means. Ukraine is running out of soldiers, and Russia is a nuclear power. The idea of an endless, financially unsustainable war—funded by billions in printed money—echoes past conflicts where the U.S. eventually had to walk away.

Yet, when it comes to Israel and Palestine, we see a glaring double standard. The same politicians who now speak about diplomacy have, for years, funded what can only be described as genocide in Palestine. Both Democrats and Republicans have blindly supported endless war and occupation, proving that neither party deserves to be taken seriously on issues of peace.

The real question is: Who benefits from war? It’s certainly not the people fighting and dying in it. Those who speak of “honor” and “cowardice” are rarely the ones sacrificing their sons—they are the ones protecting their stock portfolios, hiring PR firms to sell war as a noble cause.

If we are serious about breaking this cycle, we must reject the propaganda that war is the only option. If diplomacy is the right approach for Ukraine, why not for Palestine? If war is too costly now, why wasn’t it before? The military-industrial complex will not voluntarily step back—we have to stop buying into its justifications.

È il luogo che hanno sbagliato. Ospiti da maria de Filippi sarebbe andata diversamente 

Parodia: 

🎭 C'È POSTA PER TE – SPECIALE GEOPOLITICA 🌍

(Lo studio è in tensione. La busta è ancora chiusa. Trump da un lato, Zelensky dall'altro. Maria De Filippi, con il suo tono pacato ma fermo, cerca di mediare.)

Maria:

"Donald, Volodymyr è qui perché vuole parlarti. Vuole spiegarti il suo punto di vista. Vuoi aprire la busta?"

(Trump incrocia le braccia, sospira teatralmente e guarda il pubblico come se fosse l’unico uomo intelligente in una stanza piena di incompetenti.)

Trump: "Maria, Maria… io apro sempre le buste. Sono il più grande apritore di buste della storia. Lo sanno tutti."

(Maria fa un cenno. La busta si apre lentamente… appare Zelensky con il solito giubbotto verde militare. Il pubblico trattiene il fiato.)

IL CONFRONTO

Zelensky (serio, guardando Trump negli occhi):
"Donald, io non sono qui per litigare. Sono qui perché credo ancora che possiamo trovare un accordo che sia buono per entrambi. Io capisco che tu vuoi qualcosa in cambio del tuo aiuto… ma io ho un paese da proteggere, non un’azienda da vendere. Se firmo un accordo senza garanzie, io metto a rischio milioni di persone."

(Trump sbuffa, incrocia le braccia e alza gli occhi al cielo.)

Trump:
"Oh Volodymyr, sempre con questa storia. Guarda, io ti ho dato miliardi! BILIONI! Ti ho dato armi, soldi, persino pubblicità gratis su tutti i miei discorsi! Ma sai qual è il problema? Tu non ringrazi mai! Mai! E poi quando dico qualcosa che non ti piace, subito 'Donald mi tradisce!' "

(Maria interviene con la sua solita voce calma e diplomatica.)

Maria:

"Donald, Volodymyr sente che la sua sicurezza non è garantita. Ha paura che tu possa cambiare idea."

Trump:
"Maria, io sono l’uomo più affidabile del mondo! Lo dicono tutti! Certo, magari ho cambiato idea un paio di volte, ma questo non significa nulla! Anche Melania cambia idea su di me ogni giorno, eppure siamo ancora sposati!"

(Il pubblico ride, Zelensky scuote la testa con un mezzo sorriso. Maria si gira verso di lui con dolcezza.)

Maria:
"Volodymyr, Donald dice che ti ha già aiutato molto e che ora vorrebbe qualcosa in cambio. Tu come rispondi?"

Zelensky:
"Maria, io non voglio sembrare ingrato. Io apprezzo tutto l’aiuto ricevuto, ma devo pensare al mio paese. Se firmo un accordo che non protegge l’Ucraina, rischio che Putin mi faccia sparire dalla mappa. Donald deve capire che non è solo business, è la vita delle persone."

(Maria annuisce, poi si gira verso Trump.)

Maria:
"Donald, Volodymyr non dice che non vuole l’accordo, dice solo che ha bisogno di più garanzie. Forse non è una questione di ingratitudine… forse ha solo paura."

(Trump sospira, alza gli occhi al cielo, poi scuote la testa e si raddrizza sulla sedia.)

Trump:
"Maria… io non sono un mostro. Io voglio solo che questo accordo sia chiaro per entrambi. Se lui mi dice che può garantire che userà le terre rare per ricostruire il paese e non per fare altri debiti, allora possiamo parlarne. Io voglio vincere, ma voglio che anche lui vinca, ok? Va bene così? Lo dico una volta sola, perché io non ripeto mai le cose!"

(Maria sorride soddisfatta, poi guarda Zelensky con dolcezza.)

Maria:
"Volodymyr, Donald ti ha detto quello che voleva dirti. Ora la busta è aperta. Vuoi provare a ricostruire questo rapporto?"

(Silenzio. Il pubblico trattiene il fiato. Zelensky guarda Trump, poi guarda Maria. Fa un respiro profondo, incrocia le braccia… e finalmente sorride leggermente.)

Zelensky:
"Maria… apro la busta."

(Il pubblico esplode in un applauso. Trump allarga le braccia come a dire "Lo sapevo!", si alza e va incontro a Zelensky. I due si stringono la mano, Maria sorride soddisfatta.)

Maria:

"E anche oggi… abbiamo fatto pace. Pubblicità."

(Sigla, il pubblico applaude, mentre Trump scrive su Truth Social: “MARIA È FANTASTICA. ZELENSKY FINALMENTE HA CAPITO. THE ART OF THE DEAL!”)

🎭 FINE.

comments.text:
c'è un errore/menzogna nella narrativa di Zel sulla Crimea: non è stata invasa, ma l'autorità regionale locale ha votato a grandissima maggiranza, poi confermata con referendum, per l'indipendenza.
Non si sparò neppure un colpo!

Poi si può discutere se quell'autorità avesse o meno quel potere. E, che io sappia, l'aveva: nell'ordinamento sovietico ogni regiona autonoma aveva il diritto e potere di proclamare l'indipendenza dalla rispettiva repubblica sovietica (non dall'URSS). Quelle norme erano rimaste anche dopo la caduta dell'URSS e quindi Crimea, Abkazia, Ossezia e Nagorno Karabaq potevano separarsi da Ucraina, Georgia e Azerbajan.

Poi si può alludere a eventuali frodi e violenze elettorali. Ma tutti gli indizi ci dicono che sarebbe controintuitivo:
in 2 secoli di censimenti i russi etnici sempre maggioranza tra 69 e 72% e gli ucraini etnici minoranza tra 12 e 25%.
Nelle varie elezioni i candidati e partiti filo russi (P.delle regioni e PKU) vincevano sempre a man bassa: nel 2012 il 93% a Sebastopoli e 89,7% nel resto della Crimea

comments.text:
Hi from Ukraine! First, we thank all Europeans, Americans, and people from the rest of the world who keep expressing their support to us. Also, as a regular subscriber, thank you for keeping up more and more on the European glance on foreign affairs of the world, it shows that people should always have opportunities to form their own information bubble carefully and consciously.
It is true, that this press conference obtains a very emotional reaction here in Ukraine for a whole set of reasons. The White House is governed by emotions, that are clearly out of control, these days, and that unfortunately affects us quite directly -- example, right after this meeting, the US state department cut off their support of our energy grid restoration. Shaheds fly on us to damage it literally every day, there's in fact an air raid while I'm writing right now, and the skill of the people who work on restoring this energy grid is literally the reason I'm able to type this 😘 Thus, every shift of the mood, a falling feather if you will, ends up having direct consequences and, rather often than not, negative ones.
Second, this is another clear message and, probably, a screaming breaking point, that Europeans must lock in, cause Ukraine is just Czechoslovakia of 1938 -- others will follow if ruzzians succeed in their conquest.
And third, we want to live, freely, peacefully, and with dignity to our name, not once we've been in our dark hours, and we've learned that the only way out is by standing together, united. Tonight we are. This winter we were. These years we keep on. I've already done it myself and encourage you all to visit the website of the Come Back Alive Foundation and make a contribution to one of the ongoing projects. Every cent\penny matters. European habit, as always, sorry for possible English mistakes 😅 Love ❤

replies.author: @leefuji7459
replies.text: Man, that question from Zelen is not simple at all. If you were a political journalist, you would understand that. First, the context of the question is after JD stated that the U.S. is trying to use diplomacy to resolve the war. That was a basic response in a televised negotiation. And then, what did Zelen do? In front of the media of the entire U.S., he wanted JD to clarify what kind of diplomacy they were aiming for? Oh shit, a diplomatic issue that could end a war between two countries might cost hundreds of millions of dollars, take months, and require the effort of thousands of personnel, and Zelen wants JD to explain that in just a few sentences??? Clearly, that's a question meant to put JD in a difficult position and shows a lack of understanding of basic communication. Imagine yourself as a vice president in front of cameras having to answer a question that could require a thousand pages to explain—how would you feel then? Furthermore, Zelen's comparison of the Trump administration to the Biden and Obama administrations in terms of "standing still and doing nothing in response to Russia’s invasion in 2014" is very unreasonable. We all understand that intervening and preventing something at the start is completely different from stopping it once it's already finished. When the event is over and the invader has stabilized the situation for two years, set up defenses, and prepared for any scenarios (from 2014 to 2016), it's very difficult to intervene further. While Trump was trying to use diplomacy to help Zelen, Zelen doubted it and didn't give it serious attention by asking a trick question, which led to the escalation in the discussion. JD felt that he was thinking of a solution to help you, and then you disregarded that, which is why he said what he said. Next, Zelen’s statement that the U.S. feels secure because of the two vast oceans protecting it from enemies is incredibly stupid. It’s that statement, not the one about America potentially feeling unsafe in the future, that made Trump angry. Trump came to the presidency with the slogan ‘America First,’ which is the way he operates. It affirms the value of Americans, the value of America, and the strength of America. Then someone comes and tells you that you're strong because you have two vast oceans protecting you from dangers, how would Trump react? America’s strength clearly doesn't lie in being surrounded by the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, it lies in its military position, economy, and values. All of Zelen's mistakes destroyed the negotiations.

Once again, minerals worth $500 billion for the United States. According to the Budapest Memorandum (1994), Ukraine gave up the world's third largest nuclear arsenal in exchange for security guarantees from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia.
List of nuclear weapons that Ukraine has transferred to Russia or destroyed:
1. Nuclear warheads - about 1900 units (strategic and tactical).
2. Intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) RS-18 “Stiletto” (SS-19) and RS-22 “Scalpel” (SS-24) - 176 units.
3. Strategic bombers:
Tu-160 - 19 pcs.
Tu-95MS - 25 pcs.
Tu-22M3 - 60 units (partly utilized, partly transferred to Russia).
4. Nuclear cruise missiles X-55 - about 1100 units.
5. Launchers for intercontinental ballistic missiles - 130 silo launchers.
6. Nuclear weapons control and communication systems.
Estimates of the value of the transferred nuclear arsenal vary, but in general, Ukraine has lost at least $250-300 billion worth of weapons in 1990s prices. If we translate this amount into modern prices, the cost could be more than $500-600 billion.
What did Ukraine get in return?
Financial compensation: about $500 million from the United States.
Supply of nuclear fuel for Ukrainian NPPs in the approximate amount of USD 1 billion.
Security guarantees, which, as the 2014-2022 war showed, were not fulfilled. (tens or hundreds of thousands killed and maimed)

Objectively it makes sense for multiple reasons.

Financially China and the EU have a lot to gain from working together, the only rational actor left that can hold Putin's leish now is China and the Chinese could use European help to avoid being financially and diplomatically isolated by the Americans in case things get hot in SE Asia and avoid what happened in Russia with the sanctions. If Trump keeps pushing tariffs higher, the EU market is wealthy enough that it could absorb the excess Chinese production.

In terms of energy, the EU is pivoting hard towards renewables to reduce exposure to Russian fossil fuel. Until recently American LNG was an option but with the US turning hostile and given how much leverage it has in the gulf countries it could strangle Europe by withholding energy. China is in a similar position and to protect themselves they built a gigantic solar and battery storage industry. Europe could use this excess Chinese production to transition to renewables and the US wouldn't be able to bully China to stop like they could the gulf states.

If the US is hostile now then a strategic repositioning of Europe becomes critical for survival.

Ik begrijp dat de situatie in Oekraïne erg moeilijk is, maar ik denk dat wij ons niet moeten laten betrekken in een conflict dat niet direct onze eigen belangen raakt. 
Als Poetin Oekraïne wil hebben, is dat zijn probleem, niet het onze. 
Wij moeten ons focussen op onze eigen veiligheid, economie en welvaart, in plaats van ons te laten meeslepen in een conflict dat ons uiteindelijk meer kan kosten dan het oplevert.
Oekraïne behoort tot de armste landen van Europa, het is niet nodig dat wij ons in dit conflict mengen. 
Wij hebben genoeg eigen problemen om ons op te concentreren. 
Als politici zo graag aan oorlogsvoering willen deelnemen, laten ze dat dan zelf doen, zonder de bevolking hierin te betrekken. 
Wij hebben geen behoefte aan extra spanning, uitgaven en risico's. 
Het is tijd om ons te concentreren op onze eigen problemen en onze eigen toekomst, in plaats van ons te laten betrekken in een conflict dat niet direct onze eigen belangen raakt.

Once again, minerals worth $500 billion for the United States. According to the Budapest Memorandum (1994), Ukraine gave up the world's third largest nuclear arsenal in exchange for security guarantees from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia.
List of nuclear weapons that Ukraine has transferred to Russia or destroyed:
1. Nuclear warheads - about 1900 units (strategic and tactical).
2. Intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) RS-18 “Stiletto” (SS-19) and RS-22 “Scalpel” (SS-24) - 176 units.
3. Strategic bombers:
Tu-160 - 19 pcs.
Tu-95MS - 25 pcs.
Tu-22M3 - 60 units (partly utilized, partly transferred to Russia).
4. Nuclear cruise missiles X-55 - about 1100 units.
5. Launchers for intercontinental ballistic missiles - 130 silo launchers.
6. Nuclear weapons control and communication systems.
Estimates of the value of the transferred nuclear arsenal vary, but in general, Ukraine has lost at least $250-300 billion worth of weapons in 1990s prices. If we translate this amount into modern prices, the cost could be more than $500-600 billion.
What did Ukraine get in return?
Financial compensation: about $500 million from the United States.
Supply of nuclear fuel for Ukrainian NPPs in the approximate amount of USD 1 billion.
Security guarantees, which, as the 2014-2022 war showed, were not fulfilled. (tens or hundreds of thousands killed and maimed)
Instead, Ukraine lost its nuclear status and became a victim of Russia's military aggression.

comments.author: @Mohit_Nandawat
comments.text:
American aid has never been purely an act of charity—it has always served as a strategic tool to advance U.S. interests globally. The notion that America has been "robbed" by providing aid ignores the reality that global leadership comes with both responsibilities and returns. In fact, this very influence has often led to significant economic and political benefits for the U.S.

One clear example is the Marshall Plan after World War II. The U.S. provided economic assistance to help rebuild war-torn Europe, but this was not just about generosity. By stabilizing European economies, the plan created new, reliable markets for American goods, ensuring long-term economic partnerships. It also helped prevent the spread of communism, aligning European nations more closely with U.S. interests during the Cold War. The economic prosperity that followed strengthened transatlantic trade, benefiting American companies for decades.
Another example is U.S. aid to South Korea. In the 1950s and 1960s, South Korea was heavily dependent on American assistance. However, this support helped lay the foundation for its rapid economic development. Today, South Korea is one of the largest trading partners of the U.S.

So rather than seeing aid as a one-sided loss, it’s more accurate to view it as an investment—one that has consistently yielded long-term benefits for the U.S. in the form of economic partnerships, political alliances, and global stability.

While American aid has certainly brought long-term economic and strategic benefits, much of the frustration among the American people comes from the fact that these benefits have largely favored corporations rather than directly improving the lives of everyday citizens.

comments.text:
I’ve been following this very closely and here’s my analysis: 

1.	The Core Issue:
	•	Ukraine (Zelenskyy) wants security guarantees in any deal with the U.S. because Putin has a history of breaking agreements.

	•	Trump believes security guarantees would drag the U.S. into a direct war with Russia if Putin breaks the deal, potentially leading to World War 3.

2.	Trump’s Approach:
	•	He argues that past deals failed because previous U.S. presidents (Biden, Obama) weren’t respected.
	•	He believes negotiating directly with Putin will result in a ceasefire that Russia won’t break—because Trump himself is in charge.
	•	To deter Russia, he wants to strengthen U.S.-Ukraine economic ties, particularly through mineral rights deals, making Ukraine more economically linked to the U.S. and, therefore, a higher-risk target for Russia.
	3.	The Conflict in the Room:
	•	Zelenskyy has been pushing for security guarantees publicly, despite knowing that’s not Trump’s position.
	•	This frustrated Trump, leading him to confront Zelenskyy directly.
	•	JD Vance escalated tensions by snapping at Zelenskyy, which worsened the interaction between Trump and Zelenskyy.
	•	Trump bluntly told Zelenskyy that without U.S. support, Ukraine has no leverage in these negotiations.

Zelenskyy wants security commitments, but Trump refuses, believing economic ties and direct negotiation with Putin are the best path to a ceasefire. Privately, Trump likely recognizes the risk that Putin could still break the agreement, but without a formal security guarantee, the U.S. wouldn’t be obligated to intervene—effectively keeping America out of a potential World War III. The meeting became tense when Zelenskyy pushed his position publicly, leading Trump to call him out on his lack of leverage.

comments.text:
>>'The deal in which Ukraine gave up its nuclear weapons is known as the Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances, signed on December 5, 1994. This agreement was made between Ukraine, Russia, the United States, and the United Kingdom. Here’s a breakdown of the key points:
Background
 • After the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, Ukraine inherited the third-largest nuclear arsenal in the world, with approximately 1,900 strategic nuclear warheads and a large stockpile of tactical nuclear weapons.
 • While these weapons were located in Ukraine, they were controlled by Russian command systems, making it difficult for Ukraine to use them independently.
 • The international community, particularly the U.S. and Russia, pushed for Ukraine to denuclearize and join the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) as a non-nuclear state.
The Budapest Memorandum
In exchange for giving up its nuclear weapons, Ukraine received security assurances from Russia, the U.S., and the U.K.. The memorandum contained the following commitments:
 1. Respect for Ukraine’s sovereignty and existing borders.
 2. Refrain from the threat or use of force against Ukraine.
 3. No economic coercion to influence Ukraine’s political or economic policies.
 4. No use of nuclear weapons against Ukraine.
 5. Consultations if Ukraine faced threats related to these commitments.
Implementation and Aftermath
 • Between 1994 and 1996, Ukraine transferred all its nuclear warheads to Russia for dismantlement in exchange for financial compensation and assistance in removing nuclear infrastructure.
 • Ukraine also received security assurances, but not legally binding guarantees, which later became a critical issue.
Violation of the Agreement
 • In 2014, Russia annexed Crimea, violating Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
 • This act was widely seen as a breach of the Budapest Memorandum, but the agreement did not contain an enforcement mechanism, meaning there were no direct consequences for Russia.
 • The U.S. and U.K. condemned Russia’s actions but did not intervene militarily, leading many in Ukraine to feel that the security assurances were meaningless.''<<

comments.text:
This behavior from Trump and JD Vance is disappointing, but sadly not surprising. It's clear they have little respect for the president of Ukraine, whose country has been under attack, with thousands of lives lost. Zelensky was simply trying to explain the situation, highlighting that there was an agreement with Putin in 2014, which was repeatedly violated under Obama, Trump, and Biden’s administrations. As Zelensky made his case, JD Vance, following his usual pro-Trump stance, chose to push a narrative that Zelensky wasn’t grateful for America’s support. Of course, Trump echoed this disrespect, showing blatant disregard by inviting the Ukrainian president only to prevent him from speaking.

At this point, it seems clear that Trump and Vance don’t genuinely care about Ukraine. Their actions suggest a closer relationship with Putin, the very person responsible for invading Ukraine and causing immense suffering. Trump's idea of "peace" appears to be simply a surrender to Putin’s demands, which would lead to the loss of Ukrainian sovereignty. This reflects the most troubling and failed leadership, characterized by disregard for democracy and an alignment with authoritarian figures. It's a deeply troubling moment in American political history.

comments.text: Nous demandons immédiatement l'établissement de relations diplomatiques pour instaurer la paix entre l'Ukraine et la Russie. Il est essentiel de promouvoir le dialogue et la négociation afin de mettre fin aux hostilités et de construire un avenir pacifique pour les deux pays. La diplomatie doit être au centre des efforts internationaux pour résoudre ce conflit et garantir la sécurité et la stabilité dans la région. De plus, l'Ukraine a reçu 600 milliards d'euros depuis 2022, une somme considérable, alors qu'en France, de nombreuses personnes luttent pour se nourrir et se loger. L'Union européenne et Macron semblent favoriser la guerre, ce qui soulève des interrogations sur leurs véritables motivations, notamment pour maintenir l'Union européenne sans envisager un Frexit.

The United States has sent billions of dollars in aid to Ukraine—money that comes from hardworking American taxpayers. Yet, instead of gratitude, we keep hearing demands for more, as if we owe it to Zelensky and his government. At what point do we say enough is enough?

We all support the right of a sovereign nation to defend itself, but why is the U.S. always expected to take the lead while Europe does far less? Our economy is struggling, our border is a mess, and yet we’re still sending endless funds overseas while our own people suffer.

Ukraine’s fight with Russia is their war—not ours. We’ve done more than our fair share, and it’s time for other nations to step up instead of expecting America to bankroll this forever. I think Zelensky was use to negotiating with a weak demented puppet and got a wake up call.

Desde una perspectiva ética, la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Rusia es ampliamente condenada. La razón principal es que se considera una violación de la soberanía de un país independiente. Cada nación tiene el derecho de tomar sus propias decisiones sobre su política exterior y sus alianzas, como unirse a organizaciones internacionales como la OTAN. Impedir que un país haga esto mediante la fuerza o amenazas no solo es una agresión, sino que también socava principios fundamentales del derecho internacional y de las relaciones diplomáticas pacíficas.

Rusia argumenta que la expansión de la OTAN hacia el este representa una amenaza a su seguridad, pero eso no justifica el uso de la fuerza para impedir que otro país tome decisiones soberanas. De manera ética, el principio de no agresión y el respeto por la autodeterminación de los pueblos son fundamentales en las relaciones internacionales. La guerra, en este caso, ha causado una gran cantidad de sufrimiento y muertes, lo que refuerza la idea de que la diplomacia y la negociación deberían ser las vías preferidas para resolver disputas internacionales.

En resumen, desde una perspectiva ética, la invasión rusa se considera injustificable, ya que viola principios clave de soberanía, derechos humanos y el derecho internacional.

comments.text:
Desde una perspectiva ética, la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Rusia es ampliamente condenada. La razón principal es que se considera una violación de la soberanía de un país independiente. Cada nación tiene el derecho de tomar sus propias decisiones sobre su política exterior y sus alianzas, como unirse a organizaciones internacionales como la OTAN. Impedir que un país haga esto mediante la fuerza o amenazas no solo es una agresión, sino que también socava principios fundamentales del derecho internacional y de las relaciones diplomáticas pacíficas.

Rusia argumenta que la expansión de la OTAN hacia el este representa una amenaza a su seguridad, pero eso no justifica el uso de la fuerza para impedir que otro país tome decisiones soberanas. De manera ética, el principio de no agresión y el respeto por la autodeterminación de los pueblos son fundamentales en las relaciones internacionales. La guerra, en este caso, ha causado una gran cantidad de sufrimiento y muertes, lo que refuerza la idea de que la diplomacia y la negociación deberían ser las vías preferidas para resolver disputas internacionales.

En resumen, desde una perspectiva ética, la invasión rusa se considera injustificable, ya que viola principios clave de soberanía, derechos humanos y el derecho internacional.

replies.author: @artistic-menace
replies.text:
Popping back in here to reinforce my previous statement. Had a convo with my mom who is a solid (but not fanatical) Trump supporter who HATES Zelensky. Every reference she made to the video was taken from an analysis or article ABOUT the video, and it resulted in misunderstandings and a lack of context on her end.

She misquoted Zelensky based on others’ paraphrasing of what he said. She didn’t know the extent of the conversation, the ways each group talked about the issues at hand. She also has a generally bad view towards Ukraine and a really good opinion of Trump and Vance (not necessarily related to the video, but it colored her perception of it and I’m sure affected her understanding of the situation in general).

I’m not surprised. I just wish she would do what she raised me to do: pursue the whole story, and not just listen to the voices in an echo chamber.

That’s all. Thank you for the comments of agreement, it’s always hopeful to be reminded others also value truth and context.

This is a famous story from Japanese history.

A long time ago, Japan needed a revolution to modernize. This was called the Meiji Restoration. To make it happen, two powerful regions, Satsuma and Choshu, had to form an alliance. However, these two regions were enemies, and many samurai from both sides had died in battles. Because of this, even when they started talking about an alliance, neither side wanted to be the first to suggest it. Especially for Choshu, which was in a weaker political position, it was impossible to bring it up.

At that moment, a mediator named Sakamoto Ryoma said, "Isn't it unfair to Choshu?" His words encouraged Satsuma to propose the alliance first. This allowed Choshu to save face, and in the end, the alliance was formed. Thanks to this, Japan was able to modernize without more bloodshed.

If President Trump truly wants to achieve a ceasefire, he must play the role of Sakamoto Ryoma, the mediator who made peace possible.

replies.text:
Zelensky est un chef d’État par les circonstances, propulsé en politique par un contexte de rupture avec l’ancien système ukrainien. Mais il n’a pas l’instinct politique brut de Trump ni la capacité de manœuvre stratégique de Vance.

Face à des figures comme Trump et son vice-président, qui ont fait de la communication politique une arme redoutable, jouant sur les symboles, les punchlines et la mise en scène médiatique, Zelensky était en terrain défavorable. Son discours, basé sur l’émotion et l’appel à l’unité internationale, n’a pas le même impact face à des adversaires qui maîtrisent parfaitement l’art du débat conflictuel et du renversement de la narration à leur avantage.

Dans une confrontation comme celle-ci, ce n’était même pas une question d’arguments, mais plutôt de dynamique de communication. Trump et Vance savaient exactement comment cadrer le débat pour le tourner en leur faveur, et Zelensky, moins habitué à ce type de confrontation, n’avait effectivement aucune chance de s’imposer.

Once again, minerals worth $500 billion for the United States. According to the Budapest Memorandum (1994), Ukraine gave up the world's third largest nuclear arsenal in exchange for security guarantees from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Russia.
List of nuclear weapons that Ukraine has transferred to Russia or destroyed:
1. Nuclear warheads - about 1900 units (strategic and tactical).
2. Intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) RS-18 “Stiletto” (SS-19) and RS-22 “Scalpel” (SS-24) - 176 units.
3. Strategic bombers:
Tu-160 - 19 pcs.
Tu-95MS - 25 pcs.
Tu-22M3 - 60 units (partly utilized, partly transferred to Russia).
4. Nuclear cruise missiles X-55 - about 1100 units.
5. Launchers for intercontinental ballistic missiles - 130 silo launchers.
6. Nuclear weapons control and communication systems.
Estimates of the value of the transferred nuclear arsenal vary, but in general, Ukraine has lost at least $250-300 billion worth of weapons in 1990s prices. If we translate this amount into modern prices, the cost could be more than $500-600 billion.
What did Ukraine get in return?
Financial compensation: about $500 million from the United States.
Supply of nuclear fuel for Ukrainian NPPs in the approximate amount of USD 1 billion.
Security guarantees, which, as the 2014-2022 war showed, were not fulfilled. (tens or hundreds of thousands killed and maimed)
Instead, Ukraine lost its nuclear status and became a victim of Russia's military aggression.
    America's word isn't worth a penny?

It was clear that Zelensky was only trying to explain a simple fact—diplomacy has been tried before, and it failed, costing thousands of lives. His frustration was obvious because Vance, who has never set foot in the war, was talking as if Ukraine should just forget all the horrors they've been through and trust another deal. Putin has broken multiple agreements before—Budapest, Minsk, ceasefires—so why should Ukraine just believe this time would be different? Instead of answering that, Vance just talked down to Zelensky. And when Vance escalated, Trump followed his lead, like a schoolyard fight, changing his tone instead of trying to calm things down.

The problem wasn’t Zelensky. The problem was Vance and Trump refusing to acknowledge history and acting like Ukraine should just roll over and play nice. Zelensky wasn’t being difficult—he was demanding that any deal actually work this time, instead of leading to more betrayal and death.

comments.text:
Trump's recent meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has once again highlighted his lack of diplomatic finesse and respect for international allies. The encounter, which quickly devolved into a heated argument, saw Trump accusing Zelenskyy of being "disrespectful" and "not acting at all thankful" for U.S. support. This behavior is not only embarrassing for the United States but also detrimental to our global standing and efforts to maintain peace and stability.

Trump's approach to diplomacy has consistently been marred by a lack of tact and understanding of the nuances required in international relations. His impulsive and confrontational style has led to strained relationships with key allies and undermined the United States' role as a global leader. The meeting with Zelenskyy is just the latest example of Trump's inability to engage in constructive dialogue, instead resorting to personal attacks and ultimatums.

Moreover, Trump's comments suggesting that Zelenskyy is "gambling with World War III" and his demand for a deal with Russia show a alarming disregard for the complexities of the situation in Ukraine. His focus on personal gains and deal-making rather than strategic diplomacy puts global security at risk.

@@nateakins I support Ukraine in many ways, and we all have different ways of contributing to the fight for freedom. Not everyone can be on the front lines, but we can all do our part by raising awareness, offering support, and standing up for justice. I choose to do so by showing my support and spreading positive messages. I have the utmost respect for the soldiers fighting on the front lines. Shame on you! 

You demanded gratitude from a leader whose country is fighting for survival. You escalated a discussion that should have been about strategy and support, turning it into a public spectacle of humiliation.

comments.author: @anahelenadonascimento9231
comments.text: Que situação horrível . Fiquei incomodada e consternada pela posição de Zelenski na discussão . Sendo que não considero que Zelenski tenha sido humilhado , que foi a avaliação que vi , agora há pouco , por parte dos analistas de política internacional na Globonews -- até Demétrio Magnolli reapareceu hoje e considerou que houve humilhação . Eu considerei que tanto Donald Trump quanto JD Vance foram cuidadosos nas palavras . A questão é que a situação em si é inescapávelmente humilhante . Donald Trump é mercantilista ao extremo e deixa de lado qualquer recurso moral em nome de fazer negócios vantajosos para os EUA . Ele parece querer aplicar à uma chefia de Estado a mesma mentalidade de um dono de grande empresa . Trump não tem amor pela política , seu encantamento é restrito ao mundo dos negócios . Alguém com essa mentalidade estar no posto tão estratégico de presidente dos Estados Unidos é atordoante . O mundo está desnorteado . O tão brilhante jornalista William Waack tem chamado atenção de que parece estar havendo uma reedição da Conferência de Ialta , quando Roosevelt , Churchill e Stalin se reuniram pra fazer uma espécie de partilha do mundo -- Donald Trump parece querer dialogar exclusivamente com Vladimir Putin e Xi Jiping . Os EUA erraram em se envolver na guerra da Ucrânia sem estabelecer um limite para o apoio , que deveria ter ficado restrito à um ano , no máximo . No entanto , o erro não foi apenas de Joe Biden . Donald Trump faz de conta que não houve o apoio incondicional à Zelenski por parte , também , do Congresso americano como um todo -- seria bom que Zelenski retornasse  ao Congresso pra ver se voltaria a ser recebido com aplausos e com todos de pé . Em parte , eu entendo a hostilidade de Trump para com a Europa porque nunca foi justo que os EUA carregassem a Europa nas costas -- a questão é o modo grosseiro e estúpido na forma como Trump age . William Waack analisou que uma super potência , como são os EUA , precisa de aliados no mundo e isso para , justamente , se manter ou se sustentar como uma super potência . Não há como os EUA conciliarem a posição de super potência com a atitude isolacionista

On peut hurler de rire. Zélinsky s’est enfin pris un gros savon par le nouveau sheriff en ville et son adjoint. J’ai vaguement l’impression que Trump et Vance avaient tout programmé ainsi, avec gros clash devant toute la presse, sauf si Z avait signé le « deal », auquel cas il aurait quand même été mené dans les semaines suivantes, vers l’évidence que c’est les USA et la Russie qui écrivent seuls la suite de l’histoire. Mais le plus minable et le plus comique est Macron qui fait feu de tout bois et continue à dire que la Russie a agressé l’Ukraine alors que c’est lui Macron qui a volontairement et personnellement PROVOQUE l’invasion de l’Ukraine. En effet il a refusé d’assurer son rôle contractuel de garant de l’application des accords de Minsk et donc de protecteur de la partie russophone de l’Ukraine attaquée depuis 2014 par les Kiéviens. Puisque lui Macron reniait son obligation internationale, il a de facto obligé Poutine à tenir la sienne, en envahissant l’Ukraine pour y mener son opération de police des accords de Minsk. Avant-hier Macron s’est fait balader par Trump lors de sa visite à la Maison-Blanche et tout le monde s’en est rendu compte, même lui. Ce minable insignifiant s’est fait renvoyer avec un «bonjour à votre belle épouse» (le personnage resté à Paris). replies.text:
Zelenski fait ce que tout Chef d'Etat fait lorsqu'un autre pays déclare la guerre. Et contrairement à beaucoup d'autres il n' a pas pris la fuite. C'est un pays avec un PIB 10 fois inférieur à celui de son agresseur et qui aujourd'hui résiste toujours. Oui il reçoit des aides financières et matérielles, mais bien peu pour retrouver un équilibre des forces, et pourtant, 3 ans que ça dure et ils sont toujours là et la Russie peine à avancer. A ceux qui l'accusent d'un bain de sang en continuant cette guerre, avez vous le même regard pour 1914?

Quant aux désirs de libérer des peuples oppressés en Ukraine, je me gausse, pas souvenir que le discours fut le même avec les revendications des peuples autochtone en fédération de Russie (Tchétchénie et j'en passe...)
Celui qui joue avec la vie de milliers de gens, c'est celui qui déclenche une guerre d'occupation de territoires, chose illégale. Regardez dans combien de guerres offensives l'Ukraine a été engagée depuis la chute d' l'URSS en comparaison avec la fédération de Russie. 
Si je devais choisir un voisin, je serais plus serein avec l'Ukrainien que le Russe, bien que ce dernier a fait preuve d'une compétence militaire bien inférieure à celle qui lui était fantasmé avant le début du conflit.

Et pour conclure, lorsque vos amis sont l'Iran, la Corée du Nord, et bientôt Trump, c'est assez spécial de mon point de vue.

Humilié ? Non, juste recadré et mis de façon virile, ce qu'est censé pouvoir supporter un chef de guerre , face à la réalité . La guerre a des conséquences  terribles et hélas irréversibles  sur le plan humain , et ce des deux côtés , il y a toujours des vainqueurs et des vaincus et monsieur Zelenski fait partie de la seconde catégorie ,Game over  !  Ces personnes ne sont pas des petites filles qui jouent à la poupée en  faisant semblant de prendre le thé dans leur dinette , mais des hommes qui parlent de faire cesser une guerre et trouver des compromis acceptables pour tous. Il est évident que le président Trump pense aussi, et on ne peut le lui reprocher, aux avantages pour sa propre nation . Les Etats- Unis ont subventionné la guerre et attendent un retour  sonnant et trébuchant de leurs investissements , ce que ne fait pas l'union européenne qui  pour sa part  s'est généreusement  délestée de plusieurs milliards jetés à fonds perdus dans cette guerre . Il est aussi peut-être bon de rappeler que l' Union soviétique a payé le tribut humain le plus élevé de la Seconde Guerre mondiale avec près de 26 millions de morts ...
Mr  Zelenski embourbé dans ce conflit est ,quoi qu'il en dise ,un assisté . Envois d'armes , d'instructeurs ,déploiement de logistiques coûteuses sans parler de milliards qui lui ont été ponctuellement alloués afin de maintenir sous perfusion cette guerre perdue par l'Ukraine depuis un long moment . N'oublions pas qu'il est illégitime et a conservé son statut de président à cause de ,ou grâce à, la guerre, ce qu'espère peut-être  secrètement notre Freluquet 1er qui comme tous les européistes  est contre la paix ,et n'a de cesse que de souffler avec une opiniâtreté grandissante sur les braises de cette guerre afin que ce pitoyable  désastre embrase aussi toute l'Europe  . Ce conflit qui n'a que trop duré semble bien être, au  grand désespoir  de l'ignoble individu qui se trouve à la tête de notre pays, sur le chemin certes difficile mais non impraticable menant  à des négociations qui devront bien être consenties et surtout respectées pour que s'établisse enfin, et de façon durable,  la   paix .

Let's keep it real. This is historic. How often have we had a glimpse behind the curtain. It is a heated and very real issue...concern for all nations across the globe. In negotiation of conflict sometimes tempers flare but the intent is still the same...to resolve the issue as nonviolently as possible. We can go back and forth about today and yesterday or tomorrow....but right now matters. 

We have exhausted quite a bit from our own storehouse...and it is not without concern....but one thing is ABSOLUTELY clear...this is the one time when WE as a nation shall unite behind our president...because the possibility of war is real. Words and angst against a president because of something as trivial as a party affiliation OVER the soundness of our solidarity as a nation is a threat...a real threat to us. Feelings don't matter...because there is hurt on all sides...but this is when we grow up and America up and God bless us up....together. like him or not...we want a cease fire and an unified country before EVERYONE.

comments.text:
Former President of Poland Lech Walesa wrote the following letter to Trump.

Your Excellency, Mr. President,

We watched the report of your conversation with the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky, with fear and distaste. We find it insulting that you expect Ukraine to show respect and gratitude for the material assistance provided by the United States in its fight against Russia. Gratitude is owed to the heroic Ukrainian soldiers who shed their blood in defense of the values of the free world. They have been dying on the front lines for more than 11 years in the name of these values and the independence of their homeland, which was attacked by Putin’s Russia.

We do not understand how the leader of a country that symbolizes the free world cannot recognize this.

Our alarm was also heightened by the atmosphere in the Oval Office during this conversation, which reminded us of the interrogations we endured at the hands of the Security Services and the debates in Communist courts. Prosecutors and judges, acting on behalf of the all-powerful communist political police, would explain to us that they held all the power while we held none. They demanded that we cease our activities, arguing that thousands of innocent people suffered because of us. They stripped us of our freedoms and civil rights because we refused to cooperate with the government or express gratitude for our oppression. We are shocked that President Volodymyr Zelensky was treated in the same manner.

The history of the 20th century shows that whenever the United States sought to distance itself from democratic values and its European allies, it ultimately became a threat to itself. President Woodrow Wilson understood this when he decided in 1917 that the United States must join World War I. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt understood this when, after the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, he resolved that the war to defend America must be fought not only in the Pacific but also in Europe, in alliance with the nations under attack by the Third Reich.

We remember that without President Ronald Reagan and America’s financial commitment, the collapse of the Soviet empire would not have been possible. President Reagan recognized that millions of enslaved people suffered in Soviet Russia and the countries it had subjugated, including thousands of political prisoners who paid for their defense of democratic values with their freedom. His greatness lay, among other things, in his unwavering decision to call the USSR an “Empire of Evil” and to fight it decisively. We won, and today, the statue of President Ronald Reagan stands in Warsaw, facing the U.S. Embassy.

Mr. President, material aid—military and financial—can never be equated with the blood shed in the name of Ukraine’s independence and the freedom of Europe and the entire free world. Human life is priceless; its value cannot be measured in money. Gratitude is due to those who sacrifice their blood and their freedom. This is self-evident to us, the people of Solidarity, former political prisoners of the communist regime under Soviet Russia.

We call on the United States to uphold the guarantees made alongside Great Britain in the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, which established a direct obligation to defend Ukraine’s territorial integrity in exchange for its relinquishment of nuclear weapons. These guarantees are unconditional—there is no mention of treating such assistance as an economic transaction.

Signed,

Lech Wałęsa, former political prisoner, President of Poland

comments.author: @texaslawman2004
comments.text:
I’m a US Marine who served active duty in the 80’s and early 90’s. Back then, training had less to do with fighting terrorism and insurgents, and had everything to do with fighting Russia. Things changed after the communists were dismantled. I knew history well enough to know that it wouldn’t be long before Russia again decided that it needed to turn back time a couple of hundred years. 30 years after leaving the Marine Corps, I had an overwhelming need to be in Ukraine and help fight back against Russia. People at home didn’t understand, but people in general, have a short memory when it doesn’t involve personal issues. The rest don’t seem to recall what they learned in history class. Even worse, many Americans no longer seem to able to recognize right from wrong. It’s all about political party loyalty. Everything is either left or right. There’s very few people left in the center where the truth and common sense live.
I learned in high school the huge price our country paid after following a path of isolationism and appeasement. The politicians of the time, much like Trump, believed the world was bigger than it actually is. People looked at me like I was crazy when I told them that I was going to Ukraine to fight the Russians because I didn’t want my kids to fight in a world war. And they still don’t get it. That’s  how human history repeats over and over again. Times are more dangerous than most people realize. Trump is surrounding himself with “yes” men who will never offer any advice that Trump doesn’t want to hear. That is the complete opposite of leadership. It does cause me some anxiety to speak ill of my president because I am a Marine for life. But I have to say that he is not a smart person. I have worked many years in law enforcement and have conducted numerous interrogations. I pick up on things just from watching and listening. Trump is the opposite of most things that he brags about. If he does know anything about business dealing, he is wrong in thinking that it will, by itself, apply to foreign policy.
Ukraine needs to stop wasting time with Trump. It can continue to play along, but at the same time, Ukraine must make plans NOW to fight the Russians with Europe at its side, and not the US. If people would just research a little bit of history, they would know the future. Just pretend the year is 1939. The US can stop the world from all out war. But it won’t. There’s issues at home that are more important. We will join the war when it is too late and we will pay a high price for it. And with Trump in office, it’s hard to tell if countries in our own back yard would be allies or enemies.
I will play my small part if I can get back to Ukraine. The rest is history.

replies.author: @aguiladorada9026
replies.text: @@carlosnavarro3725 soy panameño y te explico lo siguiente porque la historia de nuestras relaciones con EE. UU se convirtió en materia académica  de estudios secundarios y universitarios. Panamá nunca cedió la soberanía a EE.UU ni siquiera en el Tratado de 1903. Así lo reconoció siempre la diplomacia norteamericana durante todo el siglo XX. DESDE el primer momento en que ese Canal estuvo operativo hasta su entrega a Panamá en 1999 Estados Unidos pagó un arriendo, y tu pagas un arriendo cuando no eres el dueño. En efecto era un usufructuario. Sí es verdad que Jimmy Carter decidió la devolución de la Zona del Canal junto con su obra de ingeniería. Pero no sé sí viviste en los 70, la presión mundial que le hizo Panamá en todos los foros del planeta fue absolutamente insoportable para el prestigio de los Estados Unidos y sin parangón para un país de su tamaño. Carter entendió que no podía distender sus relaciones con Latinoamérica si no devolvía el Canal. Por lo tanto la determinación de devolverlo se tomó antes de la negociación. Panamá no se hubiera sentado a negociar nada si no se tomaba como punto de partida que el Canal sería devuelto. ¿Para qué fue la negociación? Para determinar dos cosas: 1) el CUÁNDO. Y se decidió negociando que la devolución completa se daría en 22 años (el Tratado fue negociado en el 77, los EU se retiraron en el 99). 2) el CÓMO: la devolución sería por etapas. La primera etapa se realizó el mismo día en que entró en vigencia el Tratado: 1 de octubre del 79. Ese día EU devolvió el Cerro Ancón, el barrio de Balboa y algunas cosas más. La última étapa se completó el 31 de diciembre de 1999, cuando ya no quedaba un soldado ni una base, ni personal administrativo norteamericano. Por decisión del mismo tratado, este expiró ese mismo día pues ya el Canal y su Zona estaban por completo devueltos al país soberano. No quedaba nada por negociar ni reversibilidad pactada. El único Tratado que queda vigente es el de neutralidad. Este tampoco contempla ninguna cláusula que lo haga reversible, y sería estúpido pensar que Panamá iba a pactar dos tratados uno para recuperarlo y otro para devolvérselo a los gringos. El tratado de neutralidad, como su nombre lo indica es para la neutralización del Canal. Solo da pie a dos opciones: todos los países signatarios declaran que el Canal es neutral y se comprometen a respetar esa neutralidad. Eso es lo que ha sucedido siempre (nunca se ha cerrado, hasta declaran que Panamá lo ha manejado mejor que EU y nunca ha favorecido, en una guerra, a un beligerante sobre otro). La otra opción es que algún signatario declare que el Canal no ha sido neutral en una guerra y le ha perjudicado favoreciendo a su rival en el conflicto impidiéndole pasar. Si eso sucediera, lo más que puede decir ese país es que se reserva el derecho de atacar el Canal, pues ya no lo considera neutral). Pero eso no ha pasado. EU siempre ha ejercido su derecho de paso expedito, y sinceramente ¿creen ustedes que Panamá se lo impediría? Así que no hay fórmula de derecho que haga posible que un Canal que fue devuelto por razones de justicia ,(en las que no puedo insistir ahora) pueda ser arrebatado por EE.UU. Sencillamente sería una acción de fuerza, de guerra,  que violaría el derecho internacional y además cometería genocidio. Y se me olvidaba agregar la decisión de Jimmy Carter no solo creó tratados de consecuencias jurídicas, sino que tuvo un precedente, una base jurídica muy importante en el Acuerdo Tack-Kissinger de 1974. Allí se estableció la eliminación de la perpetuidad, que se firmaría un nuevo Tratado, que la jurisdicción norteamericana cesaría y  que el Canal y su Zona serían devueltos a Panamá entre otras cosas.
